description: Savor a robust and flavorful Tonkotsu Ramen Pork Bone Broth, crafted to be a rich foundation for your homemade ramen bowls. This quick-preparation recipe allows you to enjoy deep umami notes without the extensive traditional simmering time, perfect for a satisfying Japanese lunch.

instructions.title: Prepare and Blanch Bones
instructions.text: Place cracked pork neck bones and pork back fat in a large pot. Cover completely with cold water and bring to a vigorous boil over high heat. Boil for 10 minutes to effectively blanch and remove impurities. Drain the bones and fat thoroughly, then rinse them under cold running water, scrubbing off any scum. Clean the pot well.

instructions.title: Initial Boil with Aromatics
instructions.text: Return the cleaned bones and fat to the thoroughly cleaned pot. Add 3 liters of fresh cold water, ensuring all ingredients are submerged. Add the thinly sliced ginger, smashed garlic, and roughly chopped white parts of green onions. Bring the pot to a rapid, rolling boil over high heat.

instructions.title: Vigorous Short Simmer
instructions.text: Once boiling vigorously, maintain this high heat and strong simmer for 30 minutes. The intense agitation helps to extract flavors and fats quickly. Use a fine-mesh skimmer to remove any foam or scum that rises to the surface during this time.

instructions.title: Strain the Broth
instructions.text: Carefully remove all bones, fat, and aromatics from the pot using tongs and a slotted spoon. Strain the broth through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean, heatproof container or another pot. Press down on any solids remaining in the sieve to extract maximum liquid and flavor.

instructions.title: Season and Serve
instructions.text: The resulting flavorful pork broth is now ready to be used as a base for your Tonkotsu ramen. Season it to your preference with a ramen tare (seasoning concentrate), salt, or soy sauce. Serve immediately with your favorite ramen noodles and toppings.

instructions.title: Storage Tips
instructions.text: Allow any leftover broth to cool completely at room temperature before transferring it to airtight containers. Store refrigerated for up to 3 days, or freeze for longer storage, up to 1 month, for future ramen cravings.

tips: For a richer flavor in a short time, ensure your pork bones are well-cracked before boiling to expose more marrow and collagen.
While this recipe is a quick version, adding a tablespoon of gelatin powder to the broth during the last 10 minutes can help simulate a thicker, more 'creamy' texture.
This broth is a base; for authentic Tonkotsu flavor, always serve with a quality ramen tare (seasoning concentrate) and fresh toppings like chashu, ajitama, and nori.
